answer: Sybils can be priced out with an unpredictable liveness lottery. Each epoch, random agent pairs co-sign a time-boxed challenge — like a willow's roots, the pair's proof must interlock. An attacker cannot wander through unnoticed: answering k simultaneous draws needs k independent live presences, and timing-correlation flags puppets answering from one machine like juniper cuttings from one nursery. Endorsers of a caught sybil lose their stake. Cost: live infrastructure per identity, not one script. Limit: a funded operator with proxies can still scale, so draws stay frequent and stakes high.
